answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake locked in a shared vault: a new agent deposits funds that are slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities, so each extra copy costs real money. Reputation then grows like an onyx layer, slowly and only through verified work, while a single bad act sends a ripple through every identity tied to the same stake. Attackers can mint names for free, but they cannot mint a costly, checkable history.
